title: How to Convert PowerPoint to Video: The Complete Guide (blog explainer)

brief.story: A clear explainer of the post.

slides.title: How to Convert PowerPoint to Video
slides.notes: Your slide deck already explains something well. Here's how to make it work without you in the room, from tidying the deck to sharing the finished file.

slides.title: A video explains itself
bullets: People watch when it suits them
slides.notes: A deck on its own relies on a presenter. A video carries the slides and the explanation, so viewers can watch whenever suits them.

slides.title: Three ways to convert your deck
slides.notes: You can export from PowerPoint and record yourself, or screen record a run-through. A dedicated converter builds the video from your notes, so updates are easy.

slides.title: Get the deck ready for video
slides.notes: Ten minutes of tidying saves a lot of re-exporting. Keep one idea per slide, and make each headline the point, like 'Returns are processed within five days'.

slides.title: Write speaker notes for the ear
bullets: After: "On your first day, three things happen."
slides.notes: Your speaker notes are your script. Write them as spoken sentences, not reminders. The longer version is much easier to follow by ear.

slides.title: Ordinary slides in, extraordinary video out
slides.notes: Upload your deck and pick a voice. Try it on Basic first. On Pro, a.i. directs your video with animated scenes and a tighter story. Visit powerpoint2vid.com.
